gates.reason: Temporary fixture and database paths are generated under the OS temp directory, size and worker-count inputs are bounded, and workers receive fixed module URLs rather than executable input.
Serial and parallel row sets and assembled datasets are compared exactly before reporting, with normalized reproducibility hashes included in the summary.
The minimum-speedup environment value is converted with Number without finite positive validation, so NaN disables the benchmark failure condition.
The worker consumes only parent-supplied session descriptors, imports fixed local parsing helpers, and returns failures as structured messages without executing supplied code.
Each session is paired with its current file signature and parsed through the same row builder used by the serial control path.
The worker performs one linear pass over its parent-bounded chunk and returns rows only; the parent retains the single-writer merge policy.

findings.title: Cold-ingest benchmark accepts a NaN speedup threshold
findings.what: CHD_COLD_INGEST_MIN_SPEEDUP is converted with Number but never checked for finiteness or positivity. An invalid non-empty value becomes NaN; JavaScript then evaluates every speedup < NaN comparison as false, so even a regression below 1x exits successfully and the performance gate is silently disabled.
findings.fix: Parse the threshold with the same fail-closed bounded-number helper used for the other benchmark controls, requiring a finite positive value before creating the fixture.
findings.acceptance: A focused parser test rejects empty-invalid, NaN, Infinity, zero, and negative threshold values; running the benchmark with CHD_COLD_INGEST_MIN_SPEEDUP=garbage exits non-zero before fixture construction, while a finite positive value preserves the measured comparison.
findings.verifyNote: At the immutable baseline, line 224 yields NaN for a nonnumeric non-empty value and line 296 compares the measured speedup against it. A direct JavaScript reproduction with speedup 0.25 produced min=NaN, printed=NaN, and speedup<min=false, confirming the gate fails open.
